decisions.reason: At the homogeneous prime (x1) of k[x0,x1], the chart local ring is k[t]_(t), t=x1/x0, with residue k; ordinary localization of S instead has residue k(x0). Replaced that false formula by the degree-zero homogeneous localization quotient. Also corrected S_+=S to S_+=0 when all variables vanish, and qualified retention of nilpotents to the charts: irrelevant torsion can disappear under Proj. The chart gluing, arbitrary-field and nonreduced contracts are preserved.

The image of k[t] minus zero does not multiplicatively generate t inverse in k[t,t inverse]. However its inversion makes every nonzero fraction a unit. Replaced both set-generation assertions by explicit inverse fractions f^n/a and s/b and the localization universal property. The Laurent grading proves chart-prime correspondence; affine stalks and contraction give the overlap and base-change formulas. All four statements remain unchanged; this repairs an erroneous intermediate explanation, not a false conclusion.

Lying over needs ker(f) contained in p: Z to Z/2 and p=(3) disproves the original restatement. Added that condition to L6 and checked the actual application B=k[z1,...,zd] included in A_i has zero kernel. Normalisation plus lifting (0)<(z1) forces d=0; finite vector dimension then gives Artinian local factors and finite module length by maximal-dimension proper submodules. Also made prime-existence explicit in the existing AC-use summary. The theorem remains valid with its original hypotheses.

The resultant supplier is defined only for commutative coefficient rings; a unital map from Z to a matrix ring is permitted by the old words but its target resultant is outside that definition. Specified a commutative target in the statement, L3 and step 1.2. The Leibniz polynomial commutes with coefficient maps, e F-columns and d G-columns give the scaling powers, and the two projective coordinate cases give the chart formula including zero forms and lost leading terms.

AC was already a stated assumption and a declared dependency, so the geometric conclusions remain sound. The exclusive AC-use description omitted the irreducible-closed-subset supplier in step 4.1 and Noetherian-spectrum supplier in L10. Added both and corrected the final denial of chart Noetherianity. Height two of minimal primes, their homogeneous cores, and exclusion of chains below the irrelevant height-three maximal ideal establish nonemptiness, zero-dimensional charts and dimension-one coordinate ring over every field.
